--- Expert Track Guide ---
Compact 3.9km British circuit with dramatic elevation changes, blind crests, and the iconic Paddock Hill Bend. Natural amphitheatre setting. Technical and flowing, demanding precision on bumpy surfaces.

Corner-by-corner knowledge (use this to assess whether the driver is using correct technique):
• Paddock Hill Bend (1) [fast downhill right (T1)]: Brake after the 'two' board while slightly turning in. Blind apex — the corner drops away steeply. Late apex, let car drift to exit. TRAP: Braking too late into the blind downhill; understeer into the gravel
• Druids (2) [slow uphill hairpin (T2)]: Hard braking uphill, 1st or 2nd gear. Late apex, progressive throttle on exit. TRAP: Locking fronts on the uphill approach; early apex kills exit speed down Graham Hill
• Graham Hill Bend (3) [medium-speed downhill left (T3)]: Brake before outside kerbing starts, 2nd gear, mid-point apex. Don't cut inside kerb (causes TC/spin). TRAP: Too much inside kerb causes instability on the bumpy downhill
• Surtees (4) [uphill off-camber left (T4)]: Tricky off-camber corner — brake at the 'one' board, trail brake in. Good exit feeds long straight to Hawthorn. TRAP: Off-camber catches out — understeer on entry is common; need good car rotation
• Hawthorn Bend (5) [fastest corner on circuit (T5)]: Brake before 'one' board, 3rd-4th gear, trail brake to inside kerb. Turn in early, hug inside, get on throttle ASAP. TRAP: Not committing to the speed — hesitation here costs hugely
• Westfield Bend (6) [medium-fast right (T6)]: Brake at 'one' board, 3rd gear, trail brake in. Cut inside kerb, use all exit kerb and matting. TRAP: Not using enough kerb — track limits are lenient here, exploit them
• Sheene Curve (8) [fast right-left (T7-T8)]: Smooth direction changes at speed, carry momentum through both parts. TRAP: Over-driving causes snap on direction change
• Clark Curve (10) [fast left leading to Paddock Hill (T9)]: Clean exit onto start/finish straight — exit speed is critical. TRAP: Running wide loses speed all the way down the pit straight

Priority corners (most impactful on lap time): Paddock Hill Bend (1), Surtees (4), Hawthorn Bend (5), Clark Curve (10)

• Turn 14-15 [fast left-right onto straight]: T15 is flat — exit speed from T14 feeds start/finish straight. TRAP: Poor chicane exit means slow final sector and pit straight

• Carousel [near-360-degree tightening corner with multiple possible lines]: Progressive, patient throttle as the corner tightens, use the largest reasonable radius. TRAP: Apexing too early leaves nowhere to go as the corner keeps tightening

Priority corners (most impactful on lap time): Keyhole, Carousel

--- Expert Track Guide ---
The ultimate test of precision — narrow, unforgiving street circuit with barriers inches from the racing line. Track position and error-free driving matter more than outright pace. Slowest average speed on the calendar.

Corner-by-corner knowledge (use this to assess whether the driver is using correct technique):
• Sainte Dévote (1) [tight right-hander (T1)]: Hard braking from the start/finish straight, clean early apex to set up the climb to Massenet. TRAP: Contact-prone on the opening lap; running wide costs the run up the hill
• Massenet (3) [fast uphill left]: Commit through the blind crest, smooth steering, trust the line to Casino Square. TRAP: Lifting on the blind crest loses momentum into Casino Square
• Casino (4) [fast, undulating right]: Ride the crest and camber changes with minimal steering correction. TRAP: Bumps unsettle the car — over-correcting here compounds the problem
• Mirabeau (5) [tight downhill right]: Firm braking on the downhill approach, late apex. TRAP: Braking too late on the downhill and missing the apex
• Fairmont Hairpin (6) [slowest corner on the F1 calendar]: Full steering lock, very low speed, precise placement to avoid the barriers. TRAP: Clipping the barrier on entry or exit — almost zero margin for error
• Portier (7-8) [tight right before the tunnel]: Late apex, clean exit is essential before entering the tunnel at speed. TRAP: Poor exit here compromises tunnel entry speed
• Nouvelle Chicane (10-11) [heavy-braking chicane after the tunnel]: Hard braking from tunnel speed, precise through the direction change. TRAP: Braking too late after the tunnel — a common overtaking-crash point
• Tabac (12) [fast left-hander]: Smooth commitment along the harbour wall. TRAP: Any correction near the wall is highly costly
• Piscine (14-15) [fast left-right-left chicane complex]: Precise, rhythmic direction changes through the barriers with no margin. TRAP: Overdriving any part of the complex risks wall contact
• Rascasse / Antony Noghès (18-19) [very tight, slow right-hander; final corner onto the pit straight]: Low speed, full commitment to the apex, patient throttle Late apex, clean exit is critical — feeds the start/finish straight. TRAP: Running wide on exit compromises the run to Antony Noghes; Compromised exit costs time all the way to the line

--- Expert Track Guide ---
The Temple of Speed — 5.8km low-downforce circuit with long straights and heavy braking chicanes. Top speed and braking stability are everything. Exit speed from slow corners feeds massive straights.

Corner-by-corner knowledge (use this to assess whether the driver is using correct technique):
• Variante del Rettifilo (1-2) [tight right-left chicane (T1-T2)]: Brake between 150m and 100m board, trail brake to late apex in T1, smooth transition to T2. Hug flat inside kerb, avoid sausage kerbs. TRAP: Braking too late and cutting the chicane; early T1 apex kills T2 exit speed
• Curva Grande (3) [long fast right sweeper]: Flat-out in most cars, use full track width, smooth steering. TRAP: Any correction at this speed scrubs massive time
• Variante della Roggia (4-5) [left-right chicane (T4-T5)]: Hard braking from high speed, aggressive downshifts, use astroturf reference for turn-in. TRAP: Bouncing over sausage kerbs destabilises the car for Lesmo approach
• Lesmo 1 (6) [medium-fast right-hander]: Keep left, brake later than you think. Use orange barrier as braking ref. Trail brake with 20% pressure into the turn. TRAP: Excessive caution here — it's faster than it looks. Running wide kills Lesmo 2 entry
• Lesmo 2 (7) [medium-speed right (tighter than Lesmo 1)]: Brake at 50m board, mid-to-late apex. Clean exit is critical — feeds long straight to Ascari. TRAP: Too tight an apex loses exit speed; use all exit kerbing and astroturf
• Variante Ascari (8-10) [left-right-left chicane (T8-T9-T10)]: Brake late but maintain control through the sequence, smooth direction changes. TRAP: Over-driving the entry compromises the final exit onto the straight to Parabolica
• Parabolica (11) [long tightening right-hander]: Brake at 100m board, late apex, progressive throttle. Exit speed feeds the longest straight. TRAP: Early apex = early throttle = massive oversteer on exit. Patience is everything here

Priority corners (most impactful on lap time): Variante del Rettifilo (1-2), Lesmo 2 (7), Parabolica (11)

--- Expert Track Guide ---
Legendary 6.2km Australian circuit with 174m elevation change. Part public road, part purpose-built. The Mountain section is narrow and unforgiving with concrete walls. Conrod Straight allows 300+ km/h before heavy braking. Demands bravery on the Mountain and precision everywhere.

Corner-by-corner knowledge (use this to assess whether the driver is using correct technique):
• Hell Corner (1) [tight right at circuit start]: Hard braking, late apex. Exit speed starts the Mountain climb. TRAP: Over-cooking entry and running wide — narrow exit
• Mountain Straight [steep uphill straight]: Full throttle up the steep climb, prepare for Griffins Bend. TRAP: Not anticipating the crest and gradient changes
• Griffins Bend (2) [fast left over crest]: Commitment over the blind crest, trust the racing line. TRAP: Lifting over the crest kills momentum
• The Cutting (3) [fast section through narrow walls]: Precision is critical — concrete walls on both sides. Smooth, committed driving. TRAP: Any correction near the walls risks contact
• Reid Park (4) [tight left-right complex]: Hard braking, precise through the direction changes. Walls are very close. TRAP: Over-driving into the first part with walls millimeters away
• The Esses (7-10) [crest at the top of the Mountain; fast downhill left-right-left sequence; fast compression into left]: Car goes light over the top — smooth inputs, let it settle Descending quickly with walls close. Rhythm and commitment, carry speed Car loads up in the dip — use the grip from compression. TRAP: Aggressive steering when the car is light = instant snap; Over-driving while descending — the gradient increases speed rapidly; Not using the compression advantage
• Forrest's Elbow (12) [tight left leading to Conrod]: Late apex is critical — feeds the enormously fast Conrod Straight. TRAP: Early apex = slow Conrod Straight = massive time loss
• Conrod Straight [very fast downhill straight]: Full throttle, 300+ km/h. Prepare braking for The Chase. TRAP: Not preparing early enough for the braking zone at The Chase
• The Chase (13-14) [left-right chicane after Conrod]: Enormous braking zone from 300+ km/h. Hard, straight-line braking, precise through chicane. TRAP: Braking too late from the extremely high speeds; ABS fade
• Murray's Corner (15) [final right-hander]: Late apex, progressive throttle. Exit speed feeds start/finish straight. TRAP: Over-committing on entry and losing exit drive

Priority corners (most impactful on lap time): Forrest's Elbow (12), The Chase (13-14), Murray's Corner (15), The Esses (7-10)

--- Expert Track Guide ---
The 'Green Hell' — a 20.8km, 73-corner ribbon through the Eifel forest with extreme elevation changes and blind crests. Demands memorisation and bravery; mistakes are severely punished by close barriers.

Corner-by-corner knowledge (use this to assess whether the driver is using correct technique):
• Hatzenbach (14-19) [fast, flowing forest section]: Commit through the blind, undulating corners with smooth steering. TRAP: Lifting unnecessarily on the blind crests loses significant time
• Flugplatz (20) [fast crest where the car goes light]: Stay smooth as the car unloads over the crest, minimal steering correction. TRAP: Aggressive inputs while the car is light causes a snap
• Adenauer Forst (22-24) [tight, technical double corner]: Firm braking, patient double-apex line. TRAP: Carrying too much speed into the tightening second part
• Fuchsröhre [very fast, dipping section]: Commit through the compression at high speed, trust the car. TRAP: Braking or lifting in the dip unsettles the car badly
• Bergwerk (36) [slow, tight right-hander after a fast section]: Hard braking from very high speed, patient entry. TRAP: Misjudging the braking point after the fast approach — a notorious accident site
• Karussell (39) [banked, off-camber left-hander]: Use the banked concrete gutter to carry speed through the corner. TRAP: Missing the banking and taking the corner conventionally loses significant time
• Pflanzgarten (52-54) [fast, undulating jump section]: Commit through the compressions and crests with smooth inputs. TRAP: The car can become airborne here — excess speed or poor line risks a big moment
• Döttinger Höhe [long flat-out straight before the final corners]: Full commitment, prepare early for the braking zone at the end. TRAP: Not preparing early enough for the heavy braking after the flat-out section

Priority corners (most impactful on lap time): Bergwerk (36), Karussell (39), Pflanzgarten (52-54)

nurburgring.ctxWithSlug:
--- Expert Track Guide ---
5.1km circuit in the Eifel Mountains. Technical first sector (Mercedes Arena), fast cascading second sector, and chicane-hairpin finale. Demands precision in slow sections and commitment in fast ones.

Corner-by-corner knowledge (use this to assess whether the driver is using correct technique):
• Castrol-S (1) [sharp downhill right hairpin (T1)]: Brake at 100m board or start of red-white kerbing. 1st gear, late apex, use all exit road. TRAP: Misjudging braking on the downhill — easy to over-shoot
• Mercedes Arena (2) [technical left-left-right sequence (T2-T4)]: T2: dab brake at grey kerbing ref, 2nd gear. Stick to inside through T3 as it tightens. T4: flick in early, short-shift to 2nd. TRAP: T3 keeps tightening — running wide here ruins T4 exit onto the straight
• Turn 5-6 [right-left chicane]: Smooth direction changes, use inside kerbs. Good exit feeds Dunlop Kehre approach. TRAP: Over-driving compromises approach to the hairpin
• Dunlop-Kehre (6) [downhill right hairpin (T7)]: Tricky braking — no clear reference point. Trail brake to early first apex, coast, then get on power for second apex. TRAP: Misjudging the downhill braking zone; no reference markers make this consistently tricky
• Michael-Schumacher-S (9) [fast left-right (T8-T9)]: High-speed commitment, smooth direction change. Carry speed through both parts. TRAP: Fighting the car with corrections instead of flowing through
• Turn 10-11 [medium-speed right-left sequence]: Good exit from T11 feeds Bit-Kurve and the fast section. TRAP: Over-driving T10 compromises T11 exit
• Bit-Kurve [fast right (T12)]: Flat-out right-hand kink, stay smooth. TRAP: Unnecessary lifting
• Veedol [fast left-right chicane (T13-T14)]: Brake between 100m and 50m, 3rd gear. Cut inside kerb T13, smash inside kerb T14 (if ride height allows). TRAP: Hitting concrete block on T13 kerb unsettles the car
• NGK-Schikane (12-13) [final right hairpin (T15)]: Hard braking, tight hairpin. Clean exit onto start/finish straight. TRAP: Braking too late and missing the apex; poor exit costs pit straight speed

Priority corners (most impactful on lap time): Castrol-S (1), Dunlop-Kehre (6), Veedol, NGK-Schikane (12-13)

fuji speedway.ctx:
--- Expert Track Guide ---
4.563km, 16 turns, clockwise at the foot of Mount Fuji. A 1.475km main straight — one of the longest anywhere — feeds the hardest braking zone on the lap, then a fast downhill middle sector, then a tight technical final third. Exit speed from the last corner sets top speed down the entire straight, so the lap is won at the end of it.

Corner-by-corner knowledge (use this to assess whether the driver is using correct technique):
• TGR Corner [sharp right-hander at the end of the 1.475km straight (Turn 1)]: Brake as late as you dare from top speed, straight-line the braking, late apex to open the exit. TRAP: Braking judgement from that approach speed is the whole corner — early braking throws away the straight, late braking locks the inside front
• Coca-Cola Corner [long decreasing-radius right]: Patience — the corner keeps tightening, so hold something in reserve and wait for it to open before full throttle. TRAP: Committing to an early apex, then having to lift as the radius closes

--- Expert Track Guide ---
High-speed, 7km flowing circuit with huge elevation changes and unpredictable weather. Rewards bravery, smooth inputs, and good exits onto long straights.

Corner-by-corner knowledge (use this to assess whether the driver is using correct technique):
• La Source [tight hairpin]: Brake hard 100m before, late apex, smooth throttle on exit — exit speed feeds Eau Rouge. TRAP: Early apex causes wheelspin on exit, ruining Kemmel Straight speed
• Eau Rouge [high-speed left-right-left with elevation]: Approach flat-out or with minor lift, minimal steering input, let the car flow up the hill. TRAP: Too much steering input unsettles the car; lifting too much costs massive straight speed
• Raidillon [blind high-speed crest]: Aim for inside kerb at crest, keep car balanced as it goes light over the top. TRAP: Running wide over the crest onto exit kerb — high crash risk
• Les Combes [medium-speed right-left-right chicane]: Brake 120m before T5, hard straight-line braking, smooth transitions through the chicane. TRAP: Excessive kerb usage on T6 causes instability and poor exit onto Malmedy straight
• Malmedy [fast right-hander]: Trail brake to late apex, use full track width on exit. TRAP: Early turn-in leads to running wide and slow exit
• Rivage [downhill hairpin]: Late apex, patient throttle — exit leads into fast section. TRAP: Braking too late on the downhill approach, missing the apex
• Pouhon [double-apex high-speed left]: Commit to the entry, carry speed through both apexes with smooth steering. TRAP: Lifting mid-corner kills momentum through an entire sector
• Fagnes [fast chicane]: Light braking, smooth direction changes, use kerbs carefully. TRAP: Over-driving causes snap oversteer on direction change
• Stavelot [double-apex right]: Late first apex, short straight, then commit to second part — exit speed is critical. TRAP: Too much speed into first part compromises second apex and exit onto Courbe Paul Frère
• Courbe Paul Frère [fast flowing left]: Near-flat off Stavelot's exit — minimal lift, let the car run out to track edge to set up Blanchimont. TRAP: Lifting early or running wide scrubs momentum all the way through Blanchimont onto the Bus Stop straight
• Blanchimont [very fast left kink]: Flat in most cars, tiny lift if needed — smooth steering only. TRAP: Any snap correction at 250+ km/h risks losing the car
• Bus Stop [tight right-left chicane]: Brake 130m before, hard and late. Clean exit feeds start/finish straight. TRAP: Over-committing on entry; poor exit loses time all down the pit straight

Priority corners (most impactful on lap time): La Source, Eau Rouge, Pouhon, Stavelot, Bus Stop

mount panorama.ctx:
--- Expert Track Guide ---
Legendary 6.2km Australian circuit with 174m elevation change. Part public road, part purpose-built. The Mountain section is narrow and unforgiving with concrete walls. Conrod Straight allows 300+ km/h before heavy braking. Demands bravery on the Mountain and precision everywhere.

Corner-by-corner knowledge (use this to assess whether the driver is using correct technique):
• Hell Corner [tight right at circuit start]: Hard braking, late apex. Exit speed starts the Mountain climb. TRAP: Over-cooking entry and running wide — narrow exit
• Mountain Straight [steep uphill straight]: Full throttle up the steep climb, prepare for Griffins Bend. TRAP: Not anticipating the crest and gradient changes
• Griffins Bend [fast left over crest]: Commitment over the blind crest, trust the racing line. TRAP: Lifting over the crest kills momentum
• The Cutting [fast section through narrow walls]: Precision is critical — concrete walls on both sides. Smooth, committed driving. TRAP: Any correction near the walls risks contact
• Reid Park [tight left-right complex]: Hard braking, precise through the direction changes. Walls are very close. TRAP: Over-driving into the first part with walls millimeters away
• Skyline [crest at the top of the Mountain]: Car goes light over the top — smooth inputs, let it settle. TRAP: Aggressive steering when the car is light = instant snap
• The Esses [fast downhill left-right-left sequence]: Descending quickly with walls close. Rhythm and commitment, carry speed. TRAP: Over-driving while descending — the gradient increases speed rapidly
• The Dipper [fast compression into left]: Car loads up in the dip — use the grip from compression. TRAP: Not using the compression advantage
• Forrest Elbow [tight left leading to Conrod]: Late apex is critical — feeds the enormously fast Conrod Straight. TRAP: Early apex = slow Conrod Straight = massive time loss
• Conrod Straight [very fast downhill straight]: Full throttle, 300+ km/h. Prepare braking for The Chase. TRAP: Not preparing early enough for the braking zone at The Chase
• The Chase [left-right chicane after Conrod]: Enormous braking zone from 300+ km/h. Hard, straight-line braking, precise through chicane. TRAP: Braking too late from the extremely high speeds; ABS fade
• Murray's Corner [final right-hander]: Late apex, progressive throttle. Exit speed feeds start/finish straight. TRAP: Over-committing on entry and losing exit drive

Priority corners (most impactful on lap time): Forrest Elbow, The Chase, Murray's Corner, The Esses

Silverstone Grand Prix Circuit.ctx:
--- Expert Track Guide ---
Fast, flowing 5.9km circuit that rewards rhythm and momentum. High-speed corners dominate — Maggotts-Becketts is one of the best sequences in racing. Few heavy braking zones means every tenth counts in the fast stuff.

Corner-by-corner knowledge (use this to assess whether the driver is using correct technique):
• Abbey [fast right-hander]: Lift or light brake, smooth turn-in, use bump on apex as reference. TRAP: Using too much exit road compromises Farm entry
• Farm [fast left-hander]: Flat or near-flat, smooth inputs, three red kerbs mark apex. TRAP: Sudden lift-off causes lift-off oversteer at high speed
• Village [medium-speed right]: First real braking zone — hard braking, late apex for good exit into The Loop. TRAP: Early apex leads to running wide and slow Loop entry
• The Loop [slow hairpin (slowest corner)]: Patient entry, late apex, progressive throttle — exit onto Wellington Straight is critical. TRAP: Early throttle causes wheelspin; poor exit loses time on the entire straight
• Aintree [medium-speed sweeper]: Carry momentum from Loop exit, late apex. TRAP: Over-slowing kills Wellington Straight speed
• Brooklands [slow left-hander]: Hard braking, late apex, clean exit for Luffield. TRAP: Braking too deep and missing the apex
• Luffield [long slow left-hander]: Double apex: hit early apex, drift out, tighten for second apex. Exit speed onto Wellington is huge. TRAP: Single apex line loses exit speed onto the long straight
• Copse [very fast right-hander]: Requires commitment — flat or tiny lift, smooth steering, trust the grip. TRAP: Hesitation mid-corner scrubs massive speed
• Maggotts [fast left (part of Maggotts-Becketts)]: Quick flick left, clip apex, immediately prepare for right. TRAP: Over-driving any part of this sequence ruins the whole complex
• Becketts [fast right-left (part of complex)]: Flow through with smooth, quick direction changes — carry as much speed as possible. TRAP: Fighting the car with big steering corrections; need rhythm and commitment
• Chapel [fast right onto Hangar Straight]: Exit speed is everything — feeds the longest straight on the circuit. TRAP: Getting greedy through Becketts and arriving at Chapel offline
• Stowe [fast right-hander]: Brake in a straight line, hit the apex, use exit kerb. TRAP: Braking too late on the downhill approach
• Vale [medium-speed left]: Multiple braking references (gantry, turn-in board, entry kerb). Good exit sets up Club. TRAP: Bumpy braking zone causes lockups
• Club [fast right (final corner)]: Flat in most cars — exit from Vale is critical, long vision through the corner. TRAP: Poor Vale exit means slow Club and slow pit straight speed

Priority corners (most impactful on lap time): The Loop, Copse, Becketts, Chapel, Club
